title: Deeds & Dice
teaser: A tiny living city in the palm of your hand. Roll the dice, buy the streets you land on, raise towers block by block — and out-trade rivals who know exactly what every deed is worth. Born on a Berkeley terminal in 1980, descended from a 1904 board game about landlords.

manPage.synopsis: deeds — roll, buy and build a living miniature town on one of three boards, and out-trade rivals who reason about every deed.
manPage.description: Ken Arnold wrote monop for Berkeley Unix in 1980: a referee for up to nine people sharing one terminal, with no computer players at all and a bank that lends you what you cannot pay. Deeds & Dice keeps its rules, offers them as Berkeley 1980 beside a Standard set, and adds rivals with minds of their own, a coach, twenty-four scenarios, a Daily Deal and three towns drawn entirely in code.

howToPlay: Roll and walk the loop: buy lots you land on or send them to auction; pay rent on others'.
Own a whole district to double its rent and build on it. Trade deeds and coins between rolls.
Space roll, B buy, H build, M mortgage, T trade, E end turn, V map. Richest at the end wins.
